explanation: Already in the repo file. Earth field sites do not reproduce the Martian atmospheric pressure (about 0.6 percent of Earth sea level).

factor: Terrain mobility: slope, rock cover, step height, roughness
explanation: Relative difficulty only. Geometry of terrain (slopes, rocks, steps, roughness) can be matched to Jezero and rehearsed at Earth sites, but results show relative difficulty, not absolute passability. 30 m DEMs cannot resolve the 20 to 35 cm hazards.
Offload rig can partly compensate. A field site cannot change gravity. Normal load on the wheels is about 2.6 times higher than on Mars.

factor: Wheel sinkage and traction at Mars load
explanation: Needs offload or simulation. Embedding and slip depend on normal load and soil, so absolute sinkage and slip measured at Earth gravity do not transfer to Mars.

Class-level proxy only. Earth basalt, tephra, sand and salt crust can stand in for Jezero material classes (bedrock, cohesive soil, sand). Cohesion, grain shape and bearing strength are not matched; no bearing-strength data exist.
Vehicle differs from Perseverance. Autonomous driving, hazard avoidance and traverse planning can be rehearsed in the field. Atacama has the strongest record (Zoe, over 300 km).
Emulated, not site-dependent. Earth sites have real-time links, so delay has to be injected by the test setup. It does not depend on the site.
Separate thermal workstream. Earth field sites overlap only part of the Mars temperature range and have a different atmosphere, so thermal effects cannot be fully rehearsed on site.
Not covered. Mars dust properties and electrostatic behaviour are not reproduced by Earth soils.
Not covered. Earth sites have a protective atmosphere and magnetic field.
